Damonitu.notes: Read from the installed 2.3.0 binary, which carries full C++ symbols, beside the maker's README at github.com/phestrada/OME. Two faults are worth knowing. First, a second ParamWidget for the Tempo CV trimmer is built at the very end of DamonituWidget's constructor (a BefacoTinyKnob at 0x11078) and given the position of the end-of-cycle output jack, so the panel carries two widgets for parameter 4 and the eoc jack has a knob drawn on top of it; the library screenshot shows the knob there. The help click still resolves to the jack, because the port's box is the smaller of the two, but a mouse drag reaches the knob first. Second, every one of the eight CV inputs MULTIPLIES its knob by the incoming voltage rather than adding to it (calculateTrimmedValues, 0xf504 onward), so a patched cable sitting at 0V drives the parameter to its clamp floor. The root and octave CVs carry one further special case: when their knob is at zero the jack sets the value on its own. Two parameter tooltips are stale — parameter 11 is the pattern trimmer but is named Division CV, and parameter 19 is the steps trimmer but is named Size CV. Inputs 7 and 9 were never passed to configInput, so they hover with no name; they are the octave and chord CV inputs. Parameters 1, 2 and 3 were never passed to configParam either, so the clock, run and reset buttons hover with no name, but Module::config gives them a working 0-to-1 quantity, so they do work. The README calls the control under the clock jack a light; the code reads it as a manual step button at 0x94bc. The internal clock is an exponential of the tempo parameter, 60 BPM at the default, and it is used only when nothing is patched to the clock input.

Tezca.notes: Read from the installed 2.3.0 binary beside the maker's README. The four CV inputs multiply their knobs rather than adding to them, the same pattern as Damonitu: mutateChord reads inputs[0..2].channels at 0x1f268 and substitutes a factor of one when the jack is empty, so a cable resting at 0V pulls the parameter to its clamp floor. The module returns early from process while the clock input is empty (0x1e9dc), so it does nothing at all with no clock patched. The bass output really is an octave below the chord: BartokLab::getChordFromAxis stores note minus twelve as element zero of the chord vector at 0x5428, and the chord output's channel loop begins at element one, so the bass note is not repeated there. The README lists the voicings as default, rootless, open and three notes; the binary's strings are DEFAULT, OPEN, ROOTLESS and THREE NOTES, and the order of the last two could not be settled from the disassembly, so the line names them without claiming an order. The bass inversion parameter is configured 1 to 3 rather than 0 to 2, and the display names its three settings ROOT, 1ST INV and 2ND INV.

Chooses the rhythm: UNF spreads the hits evenly, EUC spreads them as a Euclidean pattern, PRM puts them on prime-numbered pulses, WBE on the weak beats, SBE on the strong beats and RND at random

Masino.notes: Read from the installed 2.3.0 binary beside the maker's README. Maŝino's five CV inputs do not modulate their knobs, they overwrite them: each one clamps the incoming voltage to 0 to 5V, quantises it with rmlab::RythMeloLab::quantize and stores the result straight into the Param, so the knob visibly moves to the voltage and cannot be turned while the cable is in. The clock input's rising threshold is 1V while the reset input's is 2V, so a weak clock will run the module when an equally weak reset will not. The pitch input is genuinely polyphonic, with a loop bounded by its channel count at 0x169c8; every other jack reads channel one alone. The panel prints rythm, which is the maker's spelling.
